name: Resonance Sensor
description: 22-sensor parallel-field compositor where all sensors report simultaneously under arbitration rules. Bidirectional resonance graph queryable for neighbors and subgraphs. Sound, light, gravity, thermal, chemical, and consciousness channels.

core_attributes.pattern: parallel-field composition, 22-channel arbitration, bidirectional resonance graph

scope.definition: Minimum detectable field amplitude across 22 simultaneous sensor modalities in a multi-sensor fusion array — measured as signal-to-noise improvement factor relative to single-sensor baseline.

evidence.source: Fishler & Blum (1981) 'Random sample consensus', Communications of ACM 24:381-395; Kay (1993) 'Fundamentals of Statistical Signal Processing', Prentice Hall.
cross_domain_examples: Fisher information: N independent sensors improve SNR by √N — 22 sensors give 4.7× improvement
phased array radar: combining N elements coherently gives N² SNR improvement for coherent sources
multi-modal animal sensing: owls combine visual + auditory — 2 modalities give √2 threshold improvement

scope.falsifiability: If 22-sensor arrays show no statistically significant detection improvement over single sensors at equivalent aperture, sensor correlation is destroying the independence assumption.
scope.measurement_limits: SNR improvement assumes sensor independence — correlated sensors provide less than √N improvement. Parallel architecture requires careful synchronization to avoid phase-cancellation artifacts.
